newsitem.title: JORDAN: Jordan calls on Turkey to withdraw from Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Jordan calls on Turkey to withdraw from Iraq.

text.p: Jordan urged Turkey on Tuesday to withdraw its troops from northern Iraq immediately to avoid a "dangerous escalation" in the region, the official Petra news agency said.

It quoted a foreign ministry spokesman as saying Jordan was "extremely concerned over the entry of Turkish troops deep into Iraqi northern territory, in violation of Iraqi sovereignty and threatening its unity."

"The continuation of this military operation will lead to a dangerous escalation which will serve no one," the spokesman said. He added that Turkey should withdraw its forces to avoid a "deterioration of the situation."

More than 10,000 Turkish troops, allied with the Kurdistan Democratic Party, poured into northern Iraq last Wednesday in pursuit of Kurdistan Workers Party rebels who use the region as a base to launch raids into southeast Turkey.
Both sides say they have inflicted heavy casualties on each other and Turkey's cross-border incursion has drawn increasing fire from neighbouring countries.
The fighting is taking place in a Western-protected Kurdish enclave that has been out of Baghdad's control since the end of the 1991 Gulf War.
